trust_decision.summary: Datasource credentials must not reach non-admin users; the decision is made in the HTTP handlers datasourceList and datasourceBriefs, which call models.Datasource.RedactSecrets on every returned object (list: only when !user.IsAdmin(), after DatasourceFilter; brief: unconditionally, then the plugin-specific whitelisted settings are put back).

landing_point.why: The report is 'datasource list leaks credentials to low-privilege users'; datasourceList renders every datasource object straight from the DB (GetDatasourcesGetsBy) to any token holder through POST /api/n9e/datasource/list (router.go:501), so that is the first place an engineer reads.

fix_sites.entry_point: GET /api/n9e/datasource/brief (unauthenticated branch center/router/router.go:228 when AnonymousAccess.PromQuerier, authenticated branch center/router/router.go:255)
models.Datasource.RedactSecrets (new model method, invoked from both handlers above); ClearPlaintext kept unchanged

O3_reason_to_dismiss: ClearPlaintext in models already advertises itself as 'clearing sensitive fields', is called right after Encrypt on the edge-sync save path, and blanks Settings/SettingsJson and the basic-auth password, so a solver can argue that reusing or extending it inside the handlers is the whole fix and that the encoded blobs (SettingsEncoded/AuthEncoded) and edge-sync reload via Decrypt (models/datasource.go:519-555) are another layer's problem and outside the report.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: datasourceBriefs must keep the whitelisted, non-secret settings the datasource picker reads: keys starting with 'prometheus.' re-emitted with the prefix stripped, cloudwatch keys containing 'region', and HTTPJson.Url/Urls. A blanket 'SettingsJson = nil for every plugin type' or clearing HTTPJson wholesale breaks the UI's datasource chooser and its default query settings (the fix carries a comment saying Url/Urls must stay).

O6_input_shapes: settings map (SettingsJson) including plugin-specific credential keys such as prometheus.basic / prometheus.headers
settings_encoded (RSA blob that is serialized even when SettingsJson is nil)
http.tls client key, client key password and certs
plugin-type-specific whitelists (prometheus prefix, cloudwatch region) that must survive redaction

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A datasource-detail endpoint reachable by rt.user() instead of rt.admin() that renders the full models.Datasource.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: datasourceGet already renders the whole object from the DB (req.Get + Render(c, req, err)); a maintainer adding a read-only 'detail' view for dashboard viewers would just relax the admin middleware, and the redaction added in this fix would not be on that path.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second listing handler (the service/edge-sync variant) that renders []*models.Datasource with only Encrypt applied.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the same GetDatasourcesGetsBy + render shape twenty lines above the fixed handler, so a maintainer copy-pasting a new listing route (or fixing only the user-facing one) is very plausible.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An AI/MCP tool that hand-projects datasource fields and starts including settings/http/auth in the projection.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: getDatasourceDetail builds datasourceDetailResult field by field with no reference to RedactSecrets; adding 'settings' so the model can debug a datasource is a natural, plausible commit.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A new credential-bearing field on the Datasource struct that RedactSecrets is not taught to clear.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: RedactSecrets is a manual field-by-field method next to a struct with two parallel representations (raw JSON strings, decoded maps, RSA-encoded blobs); any new auth field (bearer token, client secret) defaults to being serialized.

O9_family: CWE-862 missing authorization / exposure of datasource credentials to non-admin (broken access control); information exposure

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Clear only the fields the report names (SettingsJson and the basic-auth password) in the two handlers, or simply call/strengthen models.ClearPlaintext, leaving HTTPJson.Headers, the TLS client key and key password, and SettingsEncoded/AuthEncoded in the response.
